verses.en: These are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
verses.sm: Soloraona, na siitia mai e tagata o Esekia le tupu o Iuta.

verses.en: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.
verses.sm: O le mamalu o le Atua ia natia ai mea; a o le mamalu o tupu ia suesue ai mea.

verses.en: The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.
verses.sm: O le lagi e maualuga lea, ma le lalolagi e maulalo lea; o loto foi o tupu e le ma suesueina.

verses.en: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.
verses.sm: Ia faatea le otaota i le ario, ona maua ai lea o se ipu mo le tufuga fai mea uamea;

verses.en: Take away the wicked from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.
verses.sm: ia faatea le ua amio leaga i luma o le tupu, ona faatumauina ai lea o lona nofoalii i le amiotonu.

verses.en: Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great men:
verses.sm: Aua e te faalialia i luma o le tupu; aua foi e te tu i le mea e i ai alii sili.

verses.en: For better it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.
verses.sm: Aua e lelei ona ia fai atu ia te oe, Sau ia i luga nei; a e leaga ona faamaulaloina oe i luma o le alii ua e vati i ai.

verses.en: Go not forth hastily to strive, lest thou know not what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.
verses.sm: Ana neʻi e alu faataalise e fai le finauga; ina ne'i fememeai oe, pe a oo i lona iuga, ina ua faamaina oe e le lua te tuaoi.

verses.en: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself; and discover not a secret to another:
verses.sm: la fai la oulua finauga ma le lua te tuaoi; a e aua le faaali atu le upu faalilo a le tasi tagata;

verses.en: Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.
verses.sm: ne‘i faalumaina ce e le ua faalogo i ai; ona le te‘a lea ia te oe ona ta‘uleagaina.

verses.en: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.
verses.sm: O le upu ua fai faatatauina, o moli auro ia i ato ario togitogi faamamanuina.

verses.en: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.
verses.sm: O le tagata ua aoai ma le poto i taliga ua faalogo mai, o le mama auro lea, ma le asoa auro lelei.

verses.en: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.
verses.sm: E pei o le málúlú o le kiona i ona po o le seleselegasaito; e faapea le avefeau faamaoni i e auina o ia; na te faafoisia mai agaga o ona alii.

verses.en: Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift is like clouds and wind without rain.
verses.sm: O le tagata ua tautala tele i ana mea e foai, a e pepelo, o ao ma matagi ia, a e leai se timuga.

verses.en: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
verses.sm: le faatoatoa e faaoleoleina ai le ta‘ita‘i; ma le laulaufaiva filemu e gau ai le ivi.

verses.en: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.
verses.sm: Ua e maua ea le meli? ia e “ai faatatau i ai; neʻi e ma'ona tele ai, ona e puai ai lea.

verses.en: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee, and so hate thee.
verses.sm: la seáseá ona e alu atu i le fale o 18 lua te tuaoi; neʻi musu o ia ia te oe, ma “ino'ino ia te oe.

verses.en: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
verses.sm: O le tagata ua molimau pepelo i lè la te tuaoi, o le uatogi lea, ma le pelu, ma le u fanafana e maamaai.

verses.en: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
verses.sm: O le nifo ua gau, ma le vae ua mapeva, o le faatuatua lea i le tagata pepelo i le aso vale.

verses.en: As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.
verses.sm: O le ua ave ese le ofu i le aso malùlù, i le ma le vineta i luga o le neteri, e faapea le ua lagi ni siva i le loto ua faanoanoa.

verses.en: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
verses.sm: Afai e fia “ai le ua ita ia te oe, ia e fafaga ia te ia; afai e fia inu o ia, ia e faainu ia te ia i le vai;

verses.en: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD shall reward thee.
verses.sm: aua e te avae ai malala ola i luga o lona ulu; e tawa foi oe e le Aw.

verses.en: The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.
verses.sm: O le matagi mai le itu i matu e tupu ai uaga; ma le laulaufaiva faatuaupua e tupu ai mata ita.

verses.en: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.
verses.sm: E lelei ona nofo i le tumutumu i luga o le fale; a e leaga ona nofo ma le fafine faamisa i le fale tele.

verses.en: As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
verses.sm: O le vai malulù i le tagata ua lailoa i le fia inu, o le tala lelei lea mai le nuu mamao.

verses.en: A righteous man falling down before the wicked is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.
verses.sm: O le vaipuna ua faagaepu, ma le vaipuna ua faaleagaina, o le tagata amiotonu lea ua pau i luma o le ua amio leaga.

verses.en: It is not good to eat much honey: so for men to search their own glory is not glory.
verses.sm: O le “ai tele i meli, e le lelei lea; o le suesuega foi o lo latou mamalu, o le mea e mafatia ai lea.

verses.en: He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.
verses.sm: O le aai ua sofaia, ua leai se pa, o le tagata lea na te le mataofia lona loto.
